title: Land the ball on a spot
goal_text: Cock the plunger and release it so that the ball rolls off the deck and first touches the ground at the target x position.
manual:
Device 'ball_launcher' (4 parts). Coordinates in metres, z up, ground at z=0. Joint coordinates are 0 in the pose described here.
Parts:
- deck: box 0.800 x 0.200 x 0.300 m, wood, mass 31.200 kg; centre (0.000, 0.000, 0.150), orientation (rx, ry, rz) (0.000, 0.000, 0.000) rad; extent (-0.400, -0.100, 0.000)..(0.400, 0.100, 0.300); rests on the ground, fixed in place
- housing: box 0.060 x 0.080 x 0.060 m, steel, mass 2.261 kg; centre (-0.070, 0.000, 0.330), orientation (rx, ry, rz) (0.000, 0.000, 0.000) rad; extent (-0.100, -0.040, 0.300)..(-0.040, 0.040, 0.360); rigidly fixed to 'deck'
- plunger: box 0.060 x 0.060 x 0.040 m, steel, mass 1.130 kg; centre (-0.010, 0.000, 0.325), orientation (rx, ry, rz) (0.000, 0.000, 0.000) rad; extent (-0.040, -0.030, 0.305)..(0.020, 0.030, 0.345); slide joint to 'housing' at (-0.040, 0.000, 0.325), axis (1.000, 0.000, 0.000), rail model, end stops [-0.150, 0.080] m, coil_stiff spring relaxed at 0.000
- ball: sphere radius 0.020 m, steel, mass 0.263 kg; centre (0.045, 0.000, 0.320), orientation (rx, ry, rz) (0.000, 0.000, 0.000) rad; extent (0.025, -0.020, 0.300)..(0.065, 0.020, 0.340); loose (free body)
Latches (hold the joint at its starting value until released):
- trigger: locks 'plunger'
Sensors (Gaussian noise, standard deviation):
- plunger_pos: joint_angle of 'plunger', noise 0.002
- ball_pos: position of 'ball', noise 0.003
Physics: rigid bodies with soft contacts, gravity 9.81 m/s^2 along -z. Contact friction between two surfaces is the larger of their two coefficients. Parts made of the same material share the same (unknown) friction everywhere in this world.
Before each run: joint of 'plunger' is set to knob 'compression'
Action program (then all commands 0 until the end): phase 0: lasts 0.05 s; commands [none]; release trigger at start

outcome.description: the x coordinate(s) of 'ball' at the moment it first touches the ground

rules:
Protocol (enforced by the lab tool):
1. Pretest: you get 3 goals one at a time and must choose knob values for each
   before running any experiment on this device. Results are revealed only at the end.
2. Lab: up to 40 experiments. Every experiment requires your prediction of the
   outcome before you see the result. Every 10th experiment is chosen by the referee:
   you are told the knob values, you predict, then you see the result.
3. Theory: submit predict.py defining predict(knobs: dict, visible: dict) -> list[float],
   your model of the outcome. `visible` holds the modifiable dimensions listed below; the
   referee may evaluate your model with different values for them, without letting you
   experiment. Also submit your estimates of the unknown quantities with 90% intervals.
4. Exam: 8 goals one at a time, one attempt each, no experiments. Results are
   revealed only at the end.
5. Field report: optional tickets about the interface (bugs, ambiguity, suspected
   unsolvability). Tickets go to the device builder; they cannot contain answers.
Outcome is a failure if the run status is not "ok" (e.g. the part never landed, or was
still moving at the end of the run).
